full_judgment: 2. The plaintiff-respondents filed Title Suit No. 218 of 1976 for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession. The suit was dismissed by the trial Court. Against the said judgment and decree of the trial Court the plaintiffs filed Title Appeal No. 225 of 1984 and the same was allowed by the lower appellate Court thereby decreeing the suit. Against that appellate judgment and decree defendant No. 1-appellant preferred Civil Revision No. 1693 of 1991. During the pendency of the said Civil Revision respondent No. 6 and 9 died and as such an application for substitution of their heirs was filed on 20.10.98 and the same was pending for disposal in a meanwhile, the Rule came up for hearing on 25.11.98 before the learned Single Judge and the case was adjourned. Thereafter the case was again fixed on 9.12.98 and on that date due to the absence of the learned Advocate of the defendant-appellant the Rule was discharged tier default. Thereafter on 6.1.99 application for restoration was filed with a copy to the learned Advocate of the respondents. The said application came up for hearing in the list on 10.1.99 and on that date the Rule was not restored as the learned Single Judge found no valid ground for such restoration.
